limitations: One model/settings/platform; three repeats cannot establish significance.
Known tasks and one authored unfamiliar fixture are reported separately.
Prompt limits are transcript-audited, not enforced capability isolation.
Grading is condition-blind but method hints can remain in prose.
CLI usage is observed session usage, not billing cost or hidden provider telemetry.
Source-navigation tool access was unused in all three assigned trials; these measure assignment, not Code Slice performance.
Original deterministic exact-string and blind grading artifacts are retained. Primary post-collection review corrects free-string checks and unregistered suites-count criteria; it is not independent.
LF delivery prompts were recovered by reversing Windows CRLF display conversion and verified against original stdin hashes; original display bytes remain.
Small selected tasks and uncontrolled load cannot establish productivity, causality or monetary savings.
